firstly adverb

also first, first of all, in the first place, to begin with, above all, for starters

classical

Caes. B.G. 1.25: Caesar prīmum suō, deinde omnium ē cōnspectū remōtīs equīs (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 3.7.1
Traupman 40
Traupman 69
Traupman 61: prīmum omnium, first of all

prīmum

adverb; followed by deinde, tum, postrēmō

first, firstly, in the first place

The first of a series of points or acts: prīmum … deinde … tum … postrēmō (see secondly). prīmum omnium is “first of all”. prīmō is “at first”, as against later (prīmō … deinde), and stands for prīmum in lists mostly after Augustus (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • ante omnia — first of all, above all

    phrase · also used · classical · Quint. 1.1.4; Sen. Ep. 23.3

    What comes before everything else in importance: “above all”.

  • prīncipiō — first, to begin with, in the first place

    adverb (the ablative of prīncipium) · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.11: prīncipiō generī animantium omnī est ā nātūrā tribūtum ut sē tueātur (Lewis & Short); Traupman 108

Examples

  • prīmum est dēvium, deinde ab Autrōniō et cēterīs quadriduī, deinde sine tē.

    Firstly, it’s off the road; secondly, it’s four days from Autronius and the rest; and thirdly, it’s without you.Cic. Att. 3.7.1

  • prīmum omnium ego ipse vigilō

    first of all, I am awake myselfCic. Cat. 2.19 (Lewis & Short)

  • ante omnia nē sit vitiōsus sermō nūtrīcibus

    above all, the nurses’ speech must be free of faultsQuint. 1.1.4

  • hoc ante omnia fac, mī Lūcīlī: disce gaudēre

    do this before all else, my Lucilius: learn to be gladSen. Ep. 23.3

See also secondly, finally, then, begin.

SourcesLewis & Short: primus · Lewis & Short: primum · Lewis & Short: primo

Quintilian and Seneca from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-quintilianus, loci-seneca-epistulae); Cicero (Att. 3.7.1) as in the record secondly; the other passages as Lewis & Short quotes them.
